title: CI never builds the workspace in a default-feature configuration
description:
Three separate defects have now been found that are invisible to CI because
every gate runs --all-features:

  PKIX-6vfq  pkix-tlsrpt's tests do not compile without --all-features.
  PKIX-1hq5  pkix-ct pulls in pkix-path, and pkix-revocation-http pulls in
             pkix-revocation, unconditionally, though nothing in a default
             build uses either. Surfaced by `cargo publish`, which runs its
             verification build with default features.
  this bead  `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p pkix-ct --no-deps`
             fails with six unresolved intra-doc links — CtLog, CtLogList,
             SctVerifier::verify_sct_for_cert, ::verify_sct_for_precert,
             ::verify_inclusion, ::verify_sth — all of which are
             `#[cfg(feature = "log-list")]`. Links come from both the crate
             doc and item docs at lib.rs:131-164 and sct.rs:55/66. With
             --all-features it is clean, so pkix-ct cannot document in the
             configuration a consumer gets by default.

The pattern, not the three symptoms, is the thing to fix. quality-gates runs
clippy, test and doc with --all-features, and `cargo hack --feature-powerset
--depth 2` passes `--no-dev-deps`, which skips test targets. So no job in CI
ever compiles the workspace, its tests, or its documentation the way an
unsuspecting downstream consumer would.

Suggested minimum: add a job running `cargo test --workspace` and
`RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` with default
features. That alone would have caught all three.

The pkix-ct links specifically want `#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(...)))]`
treatment or feature-gated doc text, not link removal — the links are
correct when the feature is on.
